title: Texas foreign passport proof of identity for in-person notarization
publicBoundary: Public law and public agency guidance only. Do not add private customer facts, private provider tactics, secrets, or internal operating playbooks.
shortAnswer: Texas has a foreign-passport lane for in-person notarization when the document relates to a residential real estate transaction. Do not treat that as a blanket rule for every Texas notarization or for Texas remote online notarization.
exactTexasSosTrainingLanguage: If notarizing a document relating to a residential real estate transaction, you may accept an unexpired passport issued by a foreign country as proof of identity.

issueBoundaries.ruleUse: The Texas SOS training wording supports accepting an unexpired passport issued by a foreign country as proof of identity in this lane.
Do not assume the residential real estate wording applies. Check current Texas statute and SOS guidance before relying only on a foreign passport.

Analyze separately under Texas online notarization identity proofing and credential-analysis rules. Do not import the in-person residential real estate phrase into RON without checking the online rules and transaction record.

doNotSay: Do not say a Mexican passport works for every Texas notarization.
Do not say a foreign passport never works for Texas in-person notarization.
Do not merge in-person residential real estate wording with Texas RON credential-analysis rules.
